popups.description: A sunset overlooking the San Francisco Bay, a rooftop soirée in New York City, a flower-farm garden in Asheville, a charming plaza in Mendoza, or a luxurious hotel setting in Shanghai – these are just a few of the captivating backdrops we select to showcase the new Argentine cuisine across the globe. Our 'PopUp dinners' concept transcends traditional indoor gatherings; they are immersive experiences that seamlessly blend time and space.

section2.popupsdinners1: Since 2010, when we opened the doors of our very own home in the city of Mendoza for our first guests, we transformed our place into a hidden gem of a petite restaurant for selected guests. We’ve always had a clear vision: to share the essence of Argentine cuisine with the world.
section2.popupsdinners2: Today, our 'pop-up dinners' concept transcends mere gatherings among friends; they're immersive journeys that blend time and space. Whether it's a sunset over the San Francisco Bay, a rooftop soirée in New York, a flower-filled garden outside Asheville, a bustling plaza in Mendoza, a chic hotel in Shanghai, or an elegant art gallery in a cosmopolitan city, each locale is carefully chosen to provide our clients with an unforgettable dining experience.

section3.title: CONNECT WITH ARGENTINA
section3.description1: In each of these gatherings, we craft a multi-course menu under the premise of 'traveling cuisine' – a culinary journey where the essence of new Argentine and Latin American cuisine, influenced by Peruvian and Asian flavors, takes center stage. The backbone of the experience is a journey through a selection of Argentina's finest wine labels
section3.description2: Through our 'pop-up dinners,' we aim to have our guests connect with Argentina and its history, guided by our passion for wines and the flavors of our culinary proposal.”

aboutpablo.title: WHO IS PABLO?
aboutpablo.description: Pablo Ranea is an Argentine chef and sommelier committed to sharing the essence of Argentine and Latin American cuisine with the world. He has cultivated his expertise by apprenticing with renowned chefs across the United States, the Caribbean, Spain, Peru, and Buenos Aires. For a decade, he helmed the kitchen at Azafrán restaurant in Mendoza, where he successfully established it as one of the region's premier dining destinations. Pablo serves as a culinary ambassador for the New Argentine Cuisine, showcasing his innovative dishes in diverse locales and championing the excellence of Argentine wine throughout his travels.

section2.description1: Trained at the prestigious Gato Dumas culinary school in Buenos Aires, Pablo Ranea emerges as an Argentine chef and sommelier who has dedicated several years of his life to showcasing the best of Argentine and Latin American cuisine worldwide.
section2.description2: After several years of working and refining his skills with renowned chefs at Marriott hotels in the United States and the Caribbean, as well as other restaurants in Spain, Peru, and Buenos Aires, upon returning to Mendoza, he spent a decade at the helm of the kitchen at Azafrán restaurant. There, he successfully positioned it as one of the most acclaimed dining destinations in the region, thanks to his distinctive focus on New Argentine Cuisine.

section3.title: THE LAND OF SUN AND FINE WINE
section3.description: His profound ties to Mendoza and the viticultural world, coupled with his passion for incorporating and advocating for wines in his culinary endeavors, spurred him to attain the title of Sommelier from the Argentine School of Sommeliers in 2013. In 2016, following a successful stint at Azafrán, he opted to further immerse himself in gastronomic exploration, with a particular emphasis on instructing and championing Argentine wine in the world's foremost capitals.
section3.description2: With a solid culinary background and having created a signature cuisine with his own style, Pablo is a sort of culinary ambassador who not only brings his traveling cuisine to various destinations but is also sought after by the most prestigious culinary schools in the world. Institutions such as the CIA 'The Culinary Institute of America' (San Antonio, TX) and the ICE 'The Institute of Culinary Education' (New York, NY) have invited him to teach classes on Argentine wines to new generations of young students in sommelier and culinary programs.

section4.title: ARGENTINE WINE AMBASSADOR
section4.description1: Esteemed wineries from Mendoza, including El Enemigo, Catena Zapata, Susana Balbo, Trivento, Rutini, Nieto Senetiner, AchavalFerrer, and AWI Wines, as well as Colomé from Salta and Otronia from the Argentine Patagonia, entrust Ranea as their spokesperson and ambassador. He presents their most exclusive labels at his nomadic dinners abroad, thus introducing them to new consumers and expanding their global presence.
section4.description2: Throughout the years, Pablo Ranea has crafted a distinguished presence in the culinary world, not only within Argentina but also on the international stage. From New York, San Francisco, Houston, and Denver in the USA, to Peru, Canada, and Hong Kong, he has left his mark, cultivating a devoted following of adventurous food enthusiasts who eagerly anticipate updates on Argentine wines and revel in the delight of his exquisite creations.

classes.title: Teaching
classes.description: Throughout his journeys, with a constant focus on culinary pairings, Pablo dedicates himself to providing cooking and wine classes. Every destination he visits presents him with the chance to impart his experiences, recipes, and expertise. The Culinary Institute of America in San Antonio and California, The Institute of Culinary Education in New York, The Macao University of Science in Macao, and Urban Kitchen in Lima, Peru, have all welcomed his insightful instruction through masterclasses and cooking workshops tailored for chefs, sommeliers, the press, and the wider public alike.

partners.description: As every year, the selection of Argentine wines that Pablo presents in his tours aims to be a journey through the vast landscapes and different regions of Argentina, as well as a snapshot of the fantastic moment that the wine industry is going through.

items.a: Pablo Ranea is an Argentine chef and sommelier, trained at the Gato Dumas culinary school in Buenos Aires and certified by the Argentine School of Sommeliers in 2013. For a decade he led the kitchen at Azafrán restaurant in Mendoza, and today he travels the world as an ambassador for New Argentine cuisine and Argentine wine.

items.q: What is a Pablo Ranea pop-up dinner?
items.a: A traveling, multi-course dinner of New Argentine and Latin American cuisine, with Peruvian and Asian influences, paired with a selection of Argentina’s finest wines. Each one is held in a carefully chosen setting: rooftops, gardens, art galleries, hotels or private homes.

items.q: How can I host a pop-up dinner in my city?
items.a: Fill out the “Be a host” form or reach out by WhatsApp or email. Pablo hosts around 60 pop-up dinners a year in the cities on his tour.

items.q: How many guests does each dinner have?
items.a: On average, each gathering brings together 16 to 25 diners.

items.q: Where do the pop-up dinners take place?
items.a: Mainly in the United States (New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Houston and Denver, among others) and in Mendoza, Argentina. Pablo has also cooked in Peru, Canada, Hong Kong and Shanghai. Tour dates are published in the calendar on this page.

items.q: Does Pablo teach cooking or wine classes?
items.a: Yes. He teaches cooking, Argentine wine and food-pairing classes for chefs, sommeliers, press and the general public. He has been invited by The Culinary Institute of America, The Institute of Culinary Education in New York, the Macao University of Science and Urban Kitchen in Lima.
